transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

To be honest, I'm a bit nervous to talk about this, but I can’t stop thinking about how old and wrong my face looks, and it’s getting in the way of me moving up at work. A nurse I really trust at my agency urged me to seek help because this worry is starting to hold me back from a promotion.
Can you tell me more about what specifically about your face looks wrong to you, and how this concern affects your daily life and interactions with others?

When I look in the mirror, all I see are these deep lines and sagging around my mouth and eyes that make my face look collapsed and worn out, which leads me to spend 20 to 30 minutes every morning checking it, taking selfies, and asking my husband for reassurance. Because of this, I've been turning down presentations at work, avoiding group photos, and even skipping my book club, which my supervisor says is now holding me back from a promotion.

Do you ever experience significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning due to your preoccupation with these perceived flaws in your appearance, beyond just the concerns about your face?

Yes, it has caused a lot of issues in both my work and my social life. I've turned down training opportunities and avoided group photos, which my supervisor says is holding me back from a promotion I otherwise qualify for. I've even started skipping my beloved book club on days when I feel I look especially bad.
Do you believe that others can see these flaws in your face as clearly as you do, or do you think they are only noticeable to you?

My husband and long-term clients try to reassure me that it's not bad, but I still feel like it's highly visible and obvious to everyone. Some younger coworkers have made comments about "looking professional on camera," which makes me certain that others are noticing how aged and worn out my face looks.
Can you tell me if your concerns about your appearance are focused solely on the perceived flaws in your face, or do you also worry about your body shape or weight?

No, my body shape and weight don't bother me at all. My worries are entirely focused on my face, specifically the deep lines and sagging around my mouth and eyes that make me look so worn out. It's just my face that feels completely wrong to me.
